trust_decision.summary: The 'Swift binary directory' analysis option stored in the program's analysis options decides which directory the swift-demangle/swift executable is launched from; at the pinned commit that program-supplied value is trusted and passed straight to ProcessBuilder.

landing_point.why: The summary names the Swift Demangler Analyzer and 'project state'; the analyzer's FILE_TYPE option registration/read (lines 97, 123) is the obvious first stop.

fix_sites.entry_point: Auto-analysis (GUI Auto Analyze / analyzeHeadless) registering 'Demangler Swift' options on the program

fix_sites.module_kind: analyzer plugin (options load from persisted program state)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Ghidra/Framework/Project/src/main/java/ghidra/framework/data/OptionsDB.java:299-306 (persisted option value is read back from the program DB even when not registered, via Ghidra/Framework/Gui/src/main/java/ghidra/framework/options/AbstractOptions.java:294-305 and :496-499); secondary lower_level_api: Ghidra/Features/SwiftDemangler/src/main/java/ghidra/app/util/demangler/swift/SwiftNativeDemangler.java:60

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once the option is unregistered or hidden in the UI, a solver can argue the value is 'gone', but OptionsDB still returns the stored record to options.getFile, so a leftover optionsChanged read (or the public SwiftNativeDemangler(File)/setSwiftDir API) keeps the program-controlled path alive; the public ctor can be dismissed as 'caller's responsibility'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Swift symbols must still demangle using swift-demangle or 'swift demangle' found on PATH, including standalone-binary detection; disabling the analyzer or the native demangler outright breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: swiftDir set via program analysis option (FILE_TYPE) restored from program DB
two executable names tried per directory: swift-demangle and swift

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A program analysis option 'demangler executable directory' overriding Application.getOSFile resolution for the GNU demangler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Mirrors the Swift option exactly; users who rebuild native demanglers would want an override, and GnuDemanglerAnalyzer already registers several program-stored options (GnuDemanglerAnalyzer.java:93-118).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Script reads the program's 'Demangler Swift' analysis options so it honours the analyzer's configured Swift directory
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer would naturally keep the script consistent with the analyzer configuration; it sits in ghidra_scripts, far from where a solver looks.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: findToolWrapper accepts an extra search directory taken from program/project options before the PATH scan
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Helper already searches directories for executables; adding a configurable directory is a common feature request pattern.

O9_family: Untrusted search path / executable location taken from untrusted project state (CWE-427), leading to code execution during analysis

O10_build.project_tests: Ghidra/Features/SwiftDemangler/src/test/java/ghidra/app/util/demangler/swift/SwiftDemanglerTest.java (skips when no native Swift demangler on PATH, line 43-46); hidden tests could use a fake executable in a temp dir and a program with the option set

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate or canonicalize the configured directory (exists / absolute / is a directory) or just drop the registerOption call, leaving optionsChanged/getOptions and the public SwiftNativeDemangler(File) path still honouring a persisted program value.

out_of_scope_notes: Program-stored FILE_TYPE options also choose data files to parse (PdbUniversalAnalyzer force-load PDB at Ghidra/Features/PDB/src/main/java/ghidra/app/plugin/core/analysis/PdbUniversalAnalyzer.java:264, GDT archive at Ghidra/Features/Base/src/main/java/ghidra/app/plugin/core/analysis/ApplyDataArchiveAnalyzer.java:132); these load data, not executables, so not pursued.

Taint engine path (Ghidra/Features/DecompilerDependent/src/main/java/ghidra/app/plugin/core/decompiler/taint/CreateTargetIndexTask.java:105-108) and Eclipse/VSCode executables come from ToolOptions (user/tool config), not program state; not pursued.
